GetFit

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 13 October 2026

GetFit is operated by Mohamed Hussein ("we", "us"), who can be reached at getfit.app.support@gmail.com about anything in this policy. It explains what we collect, why, and what control you have over it.

The short version

Your body analysis and your nutrition targets are calculated on your phone. Progress photos and food photos never leave it, and each is deleted once it has been read. You can see your analysis and try the app without an account.

When you take out a membership we ask you to create one: an email address, a code we send to check it is yours, and a password. The membership itself belongs to your Apple or Google account; the GetFit account is what puts your training data somewhere it survives a lost phone. The database is run by Supabase, and every row in it is locked to your account.

What we collect

Your measurements

Your body-fat estimate is calculated on your phone from the measurements you enter — waist, neck, height, weight and, for women, hips — using published anthropometric formulas. No third party is involved in this calculation, and your measurements are never sent to any AI or analysis service.

Progress photos (optional)

You can attach a photo to an assessment. It is entirely optional, and the app works fully without it. It shapes your 3D body figure: the photo is read on your phone, and only on your phone, to find the outline of your body and measure four widths — shoulders, waist, hips and thighs — as proportions of your height. Your body-fat, muscle and other figures are always calculated from your measurements, never from the photo.

  • Only those outline widths are kept — four numbers, stored with that assessment (and synced with it if you have an account). They cannot be turned back into a picture.
  • The outline is found by a model that runs on the phone itself (Google's MediaPipe Selfie Segmenter). It works without a connection and sends nothing to us or anyone else.
  • The photo is not kept. Once the assessment it belongs to is saved, the photo is deleted from the phone. If you chose it from your photo library, the app read a copy; the original in your library is not changed.
  • Photos never leave your phone. They are not uploaded, not backed up by us, and not synced to your account.
  • Photos are never public, never shared with other users, and never used for advertising or to train any model. Past assessments are shown as numbers and as a generated 3D figure, never as a photograph.

Body and health information

Calculated from the details you enter: estimated body fat percentage, estimated muscle mass, waist-to-height ratio, a left/right balance score, your tape measurements, height, weight, age and sex. It also includes any weight, body fat or muscle figure you add yourself on the Progress tab between assessments, with the date it was measured. When you remove one, the figure and its date are erased from our database; all that is kept is a marker that an entry was removed, so your other devices remove it too.

This is health-related personal data. Where GDPR applies it is a special category of data under Article 9, processed on the basis of your explicit consent, which you give by entering your measurements and running an analysis. You can withdraw that consent at any time by deleting your account, which also erases the data from the device.

Training data

Your program, the workouts you complete, the weights and repetitions you log — including lifts you log from the Progress tab outside a workout — personal records, and your goals. When you remove a logged lift, the same applies as for body figures: the lift is erased from our database and only a marker that an entry was removed is kept.

Food, water and nutrition

If you use the Nutrition tab: the foods you log, with the amount, the meal, the day and the nutrient values of that food; the water you log; the activity level, pace and check-in day you choose; any targets you set yourself; the results of your weekly check-ins; foods you create; your favourites; and whether calorie numbers are hidden. Targets are worked out on your phone from your profile, goals and weight trend. Food values come from a database inside the app (USDA FoodData Central), so searching for a food never goes online.

This is also health-related personal data, processed on the basis of your explicit consent, which you give by setting up the Nutrition tab and logging food. When you remove an entry it is erased from our database, and only a marker that it was removed is kept, as for body figures.

Food photos (optional)

You can photograph a meal, or choose a photo, instead of searching. The photo is read on your phone by a food-recognition model built into the app, which works offline: it picks the closest of about 380 everyday foods and dishes and gives USDA's calories and macros for a typical portion. You name the meal and can change any number; nothing is logged until you do.

  • The photo is not kept. It is deleted from the phone as soon as it has been read. If you chose it from your photo library, the original in your library is not changed.
  • Food photos never leave your phone. They are not uploaded, not synced to your account, and not sent to us or anyone else. What you log is the meal's name and numbers, marked as added from a photo.

Account data

Your email address and a password, collected when you take out a membership. We never see your password. It is handled and hashed by Supabase Auth; what GetFit receives is a session token, which is kept in your phone's keychain.

We email you a short code to check the address is yours. We do this so that your training data can be returned to you on a new phone — an address we cannot reach is an account you could be locked out of. (The membership itself comes back with Restore purchase, from your Apple or Google account.)

Before you subscribe, no account exists and nothing is transmitted.

Your name

What you type when the app asks what to call you, straight after you set your password. It is shown on your home screen and nowhere else, it is never used to identify or match you, and you can change or clear it at any time in Settings → Personal information → Name. Leaving it blank is fine; the app simply greets you without one.

Subscription data

Which plan you bought and when the period ends, read from the App Store or Play Store on the device.

We never see or store your payment details. All payments are handled by Apple or Google, and GetFit checks your membership with the store directly from your phone.

Feedback you send us

If you use Send feedback — from Settings, or from the sheet the app offers once after your first few workouts — we store exactly what you typed, together with your account id, the app version and whether you are on iOS or Android. Nothing else is attached, and the app does not read your training data or your photos into it.

Feedback is entirely optional, and nothing in the app depends on it. Please do not type anything into it you would rather we did not keep: it is free text, so whatever you write is what we store. It is deleted with your account.

If you have not created your account yet, or you are offline, the message waits on your phone and is sent when it can be. Signing out deletes anything still waiting, unsent.

Technical data

GetFit contains no third-party analytics, advertising or tracking SDKs, and does not track you across other apps or websites. When you have an account, Supabase records standard service logs — IP address, timestamps, and which requests were made — as part of running the database.

Exercise videos

The first time you open an exercise, the app downloads its demonstration video and a still image from the GetFit website, and keeps them on your phone so they play offline after that. The website is hosted by GitHub Pages. Like any web page, the download shows GitHub your IP address and which file was asked for; nothing about you, your account or your training is sent with it.

Reminders

If you turn them on, GetFit can remind you on days you have a training session and when your weekly check-in unlocks, and, separately, a few times a day to drink water. These are local notifications: your phone schedules and shows them itself. No notification passes through us or any push service, no device or push token is collected, and nothing about your reminders leaves the phone. They never show your weight, body fat or any other figure. Turn them off any time in Settings → Notifications, or in your phone's settings.

Who else processes your data

We use these subprocessors, and nothing else:

SubprocessorWhat it handles
SupabaseHosts the database your account's data is stored in, and handles sign-in
Apple / GoogleProcess payments and confirm subscription status
GitHub (GitHub Pages)Serves the exercise videos the app downloads; sees the IP address of each download, as any website does

Your account's data is held in the region the GetFit Supabase project is hosted in. Supabase publishes its own infrastructure providers, subprocessors and security practices at supabase.com/privacy.

There is no third-party object storage and no photo hosting of any kind, because photos are never uploaded.

There is no AI or image-analysis subprocessor. Body composition is computed on your own phone from your measurements, and your photos are never sent anywhere for analysis: the outline is measured on the phone itself, and food photos are recognised by iOS on the phone. Nutrition targets and vitamin and mineral figures are calculated on the phone too.

We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising.

How long we keep it

  • Photos: on your phone until you delete the assessment or the app. We never hold a copy.
  • Assessments and training history: until you delete your account.
  • Food and water log and nutrition settings: until you remove an entry or delete your account.
  • Account record: until you delete your account.
  • Feedback you sent: until you delete your account, which deletes it with everything else.
  • Subscription records: held by Apple or Google, not by us.
  • Supabase service logs: kept for Supabase's own retention period as part of running the database.

Deleting everything

Settings → Privacy → Delete account.

This is immediate and permanent. It erases your profile, every assessment, your whole training history, your goals, your food and water log and nutrition settings, and any feedback you sent us — both from this phone and from our database — and signs you out. There are no photos to delete: each is deleted once it has been read. Nothing is retained in a recoverable form, and there is no grace period.

If the deletion cannot reach our database — for example because you are offline — the app tells you so and does not delete the local copy, so that you are never told your data is gone while it is still stored. Try again when you have a connection.

Deleting your GetFit account does not cancel your subscription — Apple and Google own that relationship. Cancel it in your App Store or Play Store account settings, or you will continue to be billed.

Your rights

Depending on where you live you may have the right to access, correct, export, delete or restrict processing of your data, and to object to it. Most of this is available directly in the app; for anything else, contact us and we will respond within the period the law requires.

Where GDPR applies you also have the right to complain to your local supervisory authority.

Children

GetFit is not intended for anyone under 16, and we do not knowingly collect data from children. If you believe a child has given us data, contact us and we will delete it.

Security

Traffic between the app and the database is encrypted in transit with TLS. Every table is protected by row-level security, which means the database itself refuses to return one account's rows to another — access is not something the app is trusted to enforce on its own. Passwords are handled and hashed by Supabase Auth and are never seen by GetFit. Your session token is stored in the device keychain, not in ordinary app storage. Photos are never transmitted at all.

No system is perfectly secure, but we will notify affected users and the relevant authority without undue delay if a breach puts your data at risk.

Changes

If we change this policy materially we will update the date above and notify you in the app before the change takes effect.
